listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Monday, October 12, 2026. The lead story is about federal agents searching the Washington home of Representative Ilhan Omar. The Justice Department says it approved the warrant and that the search is part of an ongoing federal investigation. Omar calls it an attempt to target political enemies. In other news, Trump said he had brokered a cease-fire to protect energy infrastructure in Russia and Ukraine. Ukrainian officials say bombs kept falling overnight on gas facilities, wounding 33 people. Saudi Arabia's minister vowed a serious response after Houthi attacks hit Riyadh's international airport, killing 13 people. The Atlanta Dream swept the New York Liberty three games to none and reached the WNBA Finals. Its opponent is the Golden State Valkyries. In tech and AI, Claude Platform added dynamic workflows for Managed Agents in beta. In politics, Breaking Points and the Majority Report cover OpenAI's investor expectations, temporary protected status, and newly leaked audio tied to Ken Paxton. In world news, NPR reports that Russia and Ukraine are both using AI-powered drones. In sports, Deebo Samuel of the 49ers will miss at least a couple of weeks with a hamstring injury. Brendan Allen beat Christian Leroy Duncan in the fifth round. In Atlanta, a European biopharma company has started the next phase of a campus in the Gwinnett County megaproject. Sandy Springs police report four arrests in a trafficking operation at local parks. In architecture, pyRevit 7 has been released, with an improved MCP server. In science, Chinook salmon are returning to the Klamath River after four dams were removed. Researchers also found a change in blood vessel cells that may help explain the Alzheimer's risk linked to APOE4. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.note: Federal agents searched the Washington, DC home of Representative Ilhan Omar, according to NPR News. The Justice Department said it approved the warrant and that the search is part of an ongoing federal investigation. Omar described the search as an attempt to target political enemies. The item does not give further details about the investigation or its scope. The Justice Department's stated reason and Omar's response are both part of the report, so readers can weigh each account directly. The story is one of the most significant domestic political developments in today's coverage. Further reporting will be needed to know what the investigation involves.
